STOCKTAKE V3 — QUICK START (Windows)
===================================

1. Keep ALL of these together in one folder (do not separate them):
      stocktake-v3.exe
      config.toml
      web\  (folder)

2. Open config.toml in Notepad and set your SQL Server details under
   [database] connection_string. Save the file.

   *** IMPORTANT — BACKSLASHES IN config.toml ***
   If your SQL Server uses a named instance like  MYPC\SQLEXPRESS  or your
   password / path contains a backslash ( \ ), you MUST handle it, because in
   a "double-quoted" value a single backslash is treated as an escape character
   and the file will fail to load. Two safe options:
      a) DOUBLE every backslash:
            connection_string = "server=tcp:MYPC\\SQLEXPRESS,1433;..."
      b) Use SINGLE quotes (no escaping needed):
            connection_string = 'server=tcp:MYPC\SQLEXPRESS,1433;...'
   (For a normal  server=tcp:<ip>,1433  connection there are no backslashes,
    so you don't need to worry about this.)

3. Double-click stocktake-v3.exe. A console window opens and stays open.
   You should see:
      Server ready. Open the address above in a browser.

4. Open the address shown (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8080) in your web browser.

5. To stop the program, close the console window.

WHAT'S NEW / IF SOMETHING GOES WRONG
------------------------------------
* The window no longer flashes and closes. If the program can't start,
  it now prints the reason and waits — "Press Enter to close this window".
  Read that message; it tells you exactly what to fix.
  - "config.toml exists but could not be parsed ... invalid escape sequence"
    means a backslash problem — see the BACKSLASHES note in step 2 above.
    The message now points at the exact line/column to fix.
  - "connection_string is empty" means config.toml loaded but the
    connection_string is blank — fill it in under [database].
  - "Could not bind to ..." means another program is using that port —
    change "port" under [server] in config.toml.

* The program now finds config.toml and the web\ folder next to the .exe
  itself, so it works no matter how you launch it (double-click, shortcut,
  or command line).

* The web UI now loads even if the database is temporarily unreachable.
  You'll only see a "Database error" inside the page when you try to load
  departments/suppliers/search — fix the connection_string in config.toml
  and the buttons start working without restarting your browser.

* Saved stock takes are written to the "stocktake_output" folder created
  next to stocktake-v3.exe (configurable via output_dir in config.toml).

* See FEATURES.md for a full description of the count file and ticket file
  formats, how they are loaded into Infinity, and the end-to-end workflow.

* **Ticket labels** — click "Ticket" on any row to mark it for label printing.
  On save, a .qry file is generated in the tickets/ subfolder. Ticketed items
  always generate a .qry even if no counts were entered. If ONLY ticketed
  items exist with zero counts, the .txt is skipped — only the .qry is written.

TIP: To see startup messages on the command line, open Command Prompt in
this folder and run:  stocktake-v3.exe
